newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fr. Tel capital may be opened autumn-Monde.
newsitem.headline: Fr. Tel capital may be opened autumn-Monde.

text.p: The French government is mulling a partial privatisation of state-owned telecoms firm France Telecom in the autumn but new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has yet to study the issue directly, French afternoon daily Le Monde said on Thursday.

Le Monde said "very good sources" had confirmed another newspaper report which said French ministers expected to partially privatise the telecoms operator later this year ahead of the liberalisation of EU telecommunications markets in 1998.
The French daily said, however, sources close to Jospin denied that the project was so advanced and said the prime minister had still to study the issue.

Le Monde also said French finance and industry minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn had explicitly told a recent closed-door meeting of Socialist members of the National Assembly that he was "not against an opening of the capital" as long as the state kept at least a 51 percent stake in the company.
Le Monde said Strauss-Kahn had two other conditions: that the workforce be consulted and further co-operation with other European firms should be kept in mind.
